decisions.reason: As a traditional rye bread close to the firm's core range, it is cheap to keep as an option and there is no clear negative signal yet that would justify abandoning it after only one year.
The premium raisin Christmas stollen is explicitly a flagship product and its gold medal is a strong positive signal, so management would almost certainly continue backing it.
The rye mixed bread with seeds fits current bread preferences and uses familiar capabilities, so despite some overlap with other breads the low cost of continuation favors keeping it.

This darker barley malt rye bread looks like the most niche and overlapping of the new breads, but with uncertainty still unresolved and continuation costs likely modest the option would usually be kept for now.
The marzipan Christmas stollen extends a seasonal category where the firm already has strength, and keeping the variant available is a relatively low-cost way to preserve upside.
Ancient grain bread was presented as a noteworthy new masterpiece and taps a differentiated artisanal theme, so the firm would likely keep the option open while learning more about demand.
